subsections.heading: Synthesis of aryl boronates

records.heading: Synthesis of 2a
records.text:
In a Schlenk-flask, 4-methoxyphenylboronic acid pinacol ester (17.56 g, 75 mmol) was dissolved in THF
(120 mL). The solution was cooled to -40 °C (acetonitrile/liq. N2 bath) and tert-butyllithium (41.2 mL,
70 mmol, 1.7 M in pentane) was added dropwise. The solution was stirred for 30 min and then warmed
to room temperature and stirred for a further 45 min before the volatiles were removed in vacuo
affording a viscous gum. Hexane was added and the mixture stirred rapidly for 1 h resulting in the
formation of a white precipitate. The solvent was removed via cannula filtration. This was purified
further by washing with hexane (3x) and then the solid dried in vacuo overnight affording the desired
product. Isolated as an air- and moisture-sensitive white solid (27.2 g, 88%). 1H NMR (400 MHz, THF-
d8) δ 7.27 (d, J = 8.4 Hz, 2H), 6.56 (d, J = 8.4 Hz, 2H), 3.65 (s, 3H), 1.13 (s, 6H), 0.84 (s, 6H), 0.63 (s, 9H);
13C NMR (101 MHz, THF-d8) δ 157.4, 133.9, 111.7, 78.5, 54.9, 30.9, 28.7, 28.2; 11B NMR (128 MHz, THF-
d8) δ 8.13. Spectroscopic data in accordance with literature.11

General Procedure 2: in situ preparation of tert-butyl aryl boronates.
In a Schlenk-flask, the appropriate arylboronic ester (0.62 M, 1.25 or 2.5 mmol) was dissolved in THF
or 2-MeTHF (3 or 6 mL). The solution was cooled to -40 °C (acetonitrile/liq. N2 bath) and tert-
butyllithium (1.0 eq., 1.7 M in pentane) was added dropwise. The solution was stirred for 30 min and
then warmed to room temperature and stirred for a further 45 min. This resulting solution was used
immediately after preparation.

In an argon-filled glovebox, an oven dried 7.5 mL vial was charged with the appropriate iron salt (0.02
M in THF, 0.5 mL, 0.01 mmol) and the appropriate ligand or ligand precursor (0.01 mmol), the resulting
mixture was allowed to stir at rt for 30 min. MgBr2·OEt2 (0.2 mL, 0.1 M in THF, 0.02 mmol), aryl halide
1 (0.1 mmol) and aryl boronate 2a (0.5 mL, 0.4 M in THF, 0.2 mmol) were then added to the vial
sequentially. The reaction mixture was then heated to 80 °C and stirred for 18 h. The resulting mixture
was cooled to room temperature and quenched with 1.0 M HCl (1.0 mL) before dodecane (internal
standard, 22.7 µL, 0.1 mmol) was added and the reaction mixture extracted into CH2Cl2 (5.0 mL). After
being thoroughly stirred, an aliquot was then taken and filtered through Celite (eluting with CH2Cl2)
and was then analysed by GC.

Under an N2 atmosphere, an oven dried Schlenk tube was charged with the appropriate boronic ester
(0.5 mmol) and then THF (3.0 mL) and the resultant solution cooled to -40 °C. tBuLi (0.29 mL, 1.7 M in
hexane, 0.5 mmol) was then added dropwise and the resultant mixture allowed to stir for 30 mins at
-40 °C. The reaction mixture was slowly brought to rt and stirred for a further 45 mins.
Meanwhile, in an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (8.6 mg, 0.025 mmol) and FeBr3 (7.4 mg, 0.025
mmol) were added to a dried Schleck tube, containing a stirrer bar, followed by THF (1.5 mL), and the
resultant mixture allowed to stir for 30 min at rt. MgBr2·OEt2 (12.9 mg, 0.05 mmol) and chlorobenzene
1a (25.5 µL, 0.25 mmol) were then added. The Schlenk tube was sealed and taken out of the glovebox
and attached to a Schlenk line and heated to an external temperature of 80 °C. The aryl boronate
formed in situ above was then added in one portion, the Schlenk was sealed, and the reaction mixture
was heated at 80 °C for 18 h. The resulting mixture was cooled to room temperature and quenched
with 1.0 M HCl (2.5 mL) and dodecane (internal standard, 56.8 µL, 0.25 mmol) was added. The organics
were extracted into CH2Cl2 (10 mL), and an aliquot was taken for analysis by GC.

records.heading: General Procedure 14: Data collection for linear free energy relationship on changing para-
substituents electrophile
records.text:
In an argon-filled glovebox, IMes·HCl (17.1 mg, 0.05 mmol), FeBr3 (14.8 mg, 0.05 mmol), MgBr2·OEt2
(25.8 mg, 0.1 mmol), dodecane (internal standard, 113.6 µL, 0.5 mmol), and aryl chloride 1 (0.5 mmol)
were added to a dried Schleck tube, containing a stirrer bar, followed by 1,4-dioxane (3.0 mL), forming
a suspension. In a separate dried Schlenk tube the aryl boronate 2b (552.9 mg, 1.25 mmol) was
dissolved in the 2-MeTHF (3.0 mL). Both Schlenk tubes were sealed and taken out of the glove box and
attached to a Schlenk line and heated to the appropriate external temperature (2-MeTHF 80 °C and
1,4-dioxane 100 °C), whilst being stirred. MeMgBr (0.05 mL, 1.0 M, 0.05 mmol) was added to the
Schlenk tube containing the pre-catalyst mixture and the resultant mixture was stirred for 5 mins. The
aryl boronate-containing solution was then added quickly to the Schlenk tube containing the pre-
catalyst mixture, which was then sealed, and the resultant reaction mixture was stirred and heated at
100 °C (external temp.). Aliquots (~0.05 mL) were taken at the times given. Each aliquot was quenched
with 1.0 M HCl (0.1 mL) and extracted into CH2Cl2 (2.0 mL) and then analysed by GC.

records.heading: Benchmarking Studies.
records.text:
In order, to determine the best functional for the single point energy calculation of all the structures
examined in the catalytic manifolds we undertook a benchmarking study based on the simplified
model compounds SM1-4 in all available spin states (Supplementary Figure 61) using Orca 5.0.3. The
geometries for each model in each spin state were optimized using the BP86 functional with a D3BJ
dispersion correction and the def2-TZVP basis set and a frequency calculation was performed at the
same level of theory. The optimised cartesian coordinates are given below. Reference energies for
each of the models were calculated using dlpno-CCSD(T1) which employs an improved iterative
approximation for the perturbative triple excitations.59 The calculations were based on the orbitals
derived for the BP86 optimiations, using def-TZVP basis sets and relativistic effects were accounted
100 for using the ZORA approximation.60-62 Two calculations were performed for each species, using the TightPNO default parameters except for the TCutPNO thresholds which were set to 1e-5 and 1e-6 in the two calculations, which allowed two point (5,6) extrapolation to the PNO space limit.63,64 Next single point calculations were performed on the BP86-optimised model structures in all possible spin states using the functionals BP86, TPPSh, wB97X, B3LYP, TPSS0, PBE0, PW6B95, PBE0-1/3, BB1K, mPWB1K, B2PLYP, mPW2PLYP, M06 and M06-2X and the def2-TZVP basis set. In all cases except PBE0- 1/3, BB1K, mPW2PLYP, M06 and M06-2X the D3BJ dispersion correction was applied. The PW6B95, PBE0-1/3, BB1K and mPWB1K functionals were obtained from LibXC.65 The single point electronic energies obtained by the coupled-cluster and DFT methods are summarised in Supplementary Figure 61. In all cases, the dlpno-CCSD(T1) calculations predict high spin (HS) ground states. While all of the functionals tested also predicted the ground state for the Fe(0) and Fe(I) models (SM1 and SM2) to be HS, BP86 and TPSSh predict an intermediate spin (IS) ground state for the Fe(III) model SM4 at variance with the coupled cluster reference results. Similarly BP86 predicts and IS ground state for the Fe(II) model SM3. The next lowest energy state predicted by the coupled cluster calculation is intermediate spin for both Fe(II) and Fe(III) models, except with TPSSh which has the HS and IS of Fe(III) reversed and BP86 which predicts HS as the second lowest energy spin state for Fe(II) and LS as the second highest for Fe(III). Examining the data in Supplementary Figure 61 it can be seen that the PBE0 functional gives the lowest unsigned variance from the dlpno-CCSD(T1) reference data (5.2 kcal/mol) which improves when only the ground state and next lowest energy state data are considered for all oxidation states (3.3 kcal/mol). In general the functional tested performed poorly against the coupled cluster reference data for Fe(II) LS with only BB1K and mPWB1K predicting the HS-LS gap to within 5 kcal/mol of the couple cluster value. At this stage we cannot rule out the possibility of the single reference coupled cluster method is failing to fully capture static correlation energy of what is intrinsically a multireference system, but note that the T1 diagnostic value (0.025) lies below the cutoff of 0.05, values above which can indicate substantial static correlation.66 It can be predicted from simple ligand considerations that low-coordinate Fe(II) complexes with only two strong field ligands are unlikely to adopt LS configurations. Thus while the calculation of Fe(II) LS electronic states appears to be problematic for the DFT functionals investigated, the LS Fe(II) pathways considered in the calculations of the catalytic manifolds are not likely to be relevant.

All calculations were performed using Orca, 4.249 or 5.0.3.50 The majority of the geometry
optimizations employed Orca 4.2 except for a few instances that proved problematic and did not
converge with 4.2 (LSIL; LSIM; LSIN; LSIO) , here Orca 5.0.3 was used employing the default grids. Orca 5.03
was also used for locating and optimising the transition states HSTSOA3 and HSTSOA4 using the ‘nudged
elastic band’ (NEB) method. The MECP calculations described were also performed using Orca 5.03 to
circumvent issues with a bug in 4.2 with the Hessian calculations; as were all benchmarking studies
examining functional performance against DFT functionals (see below).
Intermediate and transition state geometries were optimized using the BP86 functional51 with
Grimme’s D3 dispersion correction with Becke-Johnson damping,52 employing the def2-SVP basis set
on all atoms except Fe, for which the def2-TZVP basis set was used.53 The values for the integration
grid employed were Grid3, Finalgrid5 and the convergence criteria were set using tightscf. The
calculations were accelerated by the use of the RI approximation,54 employing the appropriate
Weigand’s def/2 auxiliary basis set.55 The geometries of the dimeric iron complexes investigated were
optimised first with the highest possible spin multiplicity and then the Orca ‘flipspin’ procedure was
used to generate a broken symmetry (BS) solution and the geometry optimized on the BS surface (as
verified by monitoring the expectation values of <S2> during optimization). A frequency calculation
was performed at the optimized geometry to obtain thermodynamic data and identify the nature of
the stationary state obtained. In almost all cases no imaginary frequencies were observed for the
intermediates, while single imaginary frequency stretches were obtained with transition states.
However, in a handful of cases low energy imaginary stretching frequencies were obtained, these
were for LSIA (E = - i11.75 cm-1); LSIB (E = - i23.55 cm-1); ISIE (E = - i2.6 cm-1); LSIF (E = - i9.0 cm-1); HSIJ (E = -
i15.7 cm-1); HSIK (E = - i14.2 cm-1); HSTSOA3-THF (E = - i22.0 and i14.7 cm-1) HSIM ((E = - i13.6 cm-1) and HSIU (E
= - i42.3 cm-1). In all cases the minor imaginary stretching frequency was due to the rocking of a single
Me on the IMes ligand, except for HSTSOA4-THF which displayed 2 Me rocks and ISIE which showed a low
energy aryl rock. A similar p-Me rocking feature was initially observed for a slightly higher energy
variant of the structure LSIB, which displayed a different hn interaction of the PhCl ligand (not shown; E
= - i22.25 cm-1), but in this instance we were subsequently able to resolve the issue leading to a
stationary state with no associated imaginary stretching frequencies. Importantly, this allowed us to
quantify the imaginary stretching frequency associated with the methyl rock in this instance as
contributing only 0.8 kcal/mol to the free energy (at 298 K). It is clear that the remaining observed
minor imaginary stretching frequencies associated with the methyl rocking contribute very little to
the free energy of intermediates, certainly not enough to have any meaningful impact on the
99 calculated catalytic manifolds. Subsequently the Hessian derived at STP was used to calculate the free energy correction at 373 K (the temperature of the catalytic reactions). Following identification of PBE0 as the functional of choice for energy calculations (see benchmarking below), a further single point calculation was performed on each optimized structure using the PBE0 functional56 with D3BJ dispersion correction and the larger def2-TZVP basis set on all atoms in which implicit solvent effects were also captured using the standard implementation of the CPCM method,57 with THF as the solvent. These calculations were accelerated using the RIJCOSX approximation58 employing the def/2 auxiliary basis set. For dimeric iron complexes these single point energy calculations were obtained starting from the highest multiplicity of the BS-optimized geometry followed by ‘flipspin’ to the BS solution and the expectation values of <S2> were compared with those obtained from the BS optimisation studies to ensure they lay on the same surface.
